4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: One detailed bug report with screenshots filed as a GitHub Issue on your partner's repo, the bug filed on YOUR repo fixed and signed off by the tester who found it, and ROLLER v2 pushed with a changelog on your portfolio site — all by Sunday night.
4th Period.workingNow: Getting your fix signed off by the tester, pushing v2, and writing your changelog.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can get my fix signed off by the tester who found the bug, push v2, and write a changelog that links to the Issue, so anyone can see how feedback improved my game.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.19 — Document programs in order to make them easier to follow, test, and debug.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.10 — Writing literary and informational texts to present, describe, and explain ideas and information, using appropriate technology.
agenda: Partner sign-off: re-test, check nothing broke, close Issue (10 min)
Fix anything that failed, then push v2 (12 min)
Changelog on your portfolio, linked to the Issue (13 min)
Gallery play: try a classmate's v2 (5 min)
Exit Ticket: paste your v2 link (5 min)
4th Period.connections: All week you ran a real feedback cycle: test, report, fix, verify. Today you close the loop — the tester who found your bug confirms it's gone and closes the Issue, you ship v2, and your changelog shows exactly what changed and why. Next week we leave the screen for physical engineering.

6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: Your finished game, published and embedded on your Google Site by Sunday night — with your tester notes and observer notes filled in, 1 bug fixed in your own game, and 3 sentences on what you changed and why.
6th Period.workingNow: Getting your fix checked, publishing your game on your Google Site, and writing what you changed.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can get my fix checked by my tester, publish my game on my Google Site, and write 3 sentences on what I changed and why, so anyone can play it and see how testing made it better.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.19 — Document programs in order to make them easier to follow, test, and debug.

I do: share link → embed on Google Site (5 min)
You do: publish and embed your game (18 min)

6th Period.connections: Yesterday you fixed your bug. Today the tester who found it checks your fix, your game goes live on your Google Site, and you explain how testing made it better. Next week we leave the computer and start building real structures in engineering.
